card: This pull request raises the minimum C++ standard from C++20 to C++23, bumping minimum compiler requirements to GCC 13 and Clang 19. It replaces custom polyfills such as util::Expected and byteswap implementations with standard library equivalents like std::expected and std::byteswap, while adopting modern idioms like std::string::contains and std::views::zip across the codebase. The author notes that workarounds to avoid C++23 keep accumulating while external dependencies like libmultiprocess already use C++23 features. This draft RFC is intended to unblock work tracked in #34979.
changed_since_previous: Added include-what-you-use adjustments and direct inclusions of <expected> in multiple source files to satisfy include linters.
evidence: PR description: 'the workarounds to avoid C++23 keep accumulating and some parts of the code already use C++23 features, such as lambda attributes' (linking to libmultiprocess commit bdd0cd6)
PR description: notes that requiring C++23 unlocks future features tracked in issue #34979 while bumping compiler requirements to GCC 13 and Clang 19
problem: Maintaining C++20 compatibility forces developers to write and maintain polyfills and workarounds in-tree, while dependent projects such as libmultiprocess have already begun using C++23 features.

risk.why: Bumping compiler version requirements to GCC 13 and Clang 19 can break builds on older developer systems and distros.

scope_notes: Draft RFC with wide mechanical churn: replaces string find idioms with std::string::contains across dozens of test and source files.
summary: This pull request raises the minimum C++ standard from C++20 to C++23 across CMake, depends, and CI, bumping minimum compiler requirements to GCC 13 and Clang 19. It replaces in-tree polyfills with standard library equivalents like std::expected and std::byteswap, removes obsolete workarounds like ALWAYS_FALSE, and adopts C++23 features such as std::string::contains and std::views::zip.
